ai.title: Replace terminal wrapper with Card component in Agents Quick Start
ai.summary: The Agents overview Quick Start section now uses the standard `Card` component instead of a raw terminal wrapper. This aligns the documentation with the project's UI design system and improves readability. The change is scoped to `web/src/content/agents/overview.mdx`. The new card displays the `codebuff init-agents` command within a structured `CardContent` block.

eli5.text: You can no longer edit the prompt template when creating a new agent from scratch using the assistant; the prompt is now auto-filled with a default template and must be changed later through the advanced settings in the agent configuration. This is a behind-the-scenes change to the AI coding assistant's documentation about creating autonomous agents, so you won't see it affect the model's behavior, it just makes the setup guide look neater by using a styled box around the command you type.

ai.title: Add syntax highlighting to docs code demos
ai.summary: Docs code blocks now render with syntax highlighting via `prism-react-renderer`. `code-demo.tsx` implements language alias mapping, leading whitespace trimming, and theme overrides for bash and plain text. Change scoped to `web` package.

eli5.text: When you read through our documentation and come across example code snippets, those snippets will now be displayed in full color instead of just plain black-and-white text. The website automatically applies coloring and formatting to match what each programming language looks like when you're actually writing it, so the examples are easier to follow and scan at a glance. This change is live today and only affects the documentation pages on the web.

ai.title: Fix /agents submenu to show all agents
ai.summary: The /agents submenu now displays all loaded agents instead of just those in .agents/templates. This was achieved by switching from manual directory scanning to using `getLocalAgentInfo()` and iterating over `loadedAgents`. The logic for mapping agent IDs to file paths was updated to search recursively using `getAllTsFiles`. Changes are localized to `npm-app/src/cli-handlers/agents.ts` and `npm-app/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: You use the /agents menu to explore the assistants available to you. Previously, the menu only listed assistants saved in one specific folder, so any that had been loaded for your account didn't appear. Now the menu shows every assistant currently available to you, the same set that loads when you first open your app. When you open /agents, you'll see all those assistants listed and can pick any of them to review, instead of a short list that might be missing some.

ai.title: Add 'agnet' and 'agnets' aliases to /agents command
ai.summary: Added 'agnet' and 'agnets' to the aliases array for the /agents command in npm-app/src/menu.ts. This change improves discoverability and reduces user friction by accepting common alternate spellings. The update applies to the CLI interactive menu. No migration or breaking changes.

eli5.text: When you type a command to manage your helper profiles, the system now quietly accepts a couple of the most common typos of that command name instead of rejecting them, so the command still runs without you having to correct the spelling. This is limited to the interactive menu on your computer, and it takes effect now.

ai.title: Remove efficiency metric from git evals
ai.summary: Drops efficiency scoring from git-evals pipeline, including judge prompt, types, and reporting. Removes average_efficiency and efficiencyScore from FullEvalLog and JudgingAnalysisSchema in types.ts. Strips efficiency from email summaries, post-eval analysis, and console output. Eliminates timing/cost context injection in judge prompt.

eli5.text: The internal evaluation reports that grade how well the coding assistant performs no longer include a separate score for how efficiently it works or how much each evaluation cost. If you open one of these reports now, the line for Efficiency and the cost-per-point metric are simply gone, along with the timing and cost details that used to be fed into the grading prompt. This affects only the internal team running these evaluations; nothing visible to end users changed.

ai.title: Refine git eval prompts for full spec completion
ai.summary: Judge and runner prompts in evals/git-evals require full spec satisfaction, explicitly listing tests and docs. Judge prompt drops redundant 'trace of' phrasing. Affects judge-git-eval.ts and run-git-evals.ts.

eli5.text: The system that checks whether work is truly finished got stricter about what it considers 'done.' When reviewing completed work, it now requires seeing the full picture, including test coverage and documentation, before signing off, rather than accepting partial completion. The wording it uses to evaluate results was also cleaned up to remove a redundant phrase. This affects internal quality checks, so if you were looking at how work gets graded, you'd see it now demands more complete submissions with clearer scoring criteria.

ai.title: Judge prompt restricts scoring to spec
ai.summary: Updated `buildAnalysisPrompt` in `evals/git-evals/judge-git-eval.ts` to explicitly instruct the judge to score only against the provided spec. Added a note preventing point deductions for out-of-spec items like unit tests or documentation. This ensures evaluation fairness by aligning scoring criteria with the agent's actual access constraints.

eli5.text: The internal system that rates how well our AI coding tool follows instructions now tells its evaluator to score strictly against the given task list, ignoring extras like tests or documentation. This matters only to teams running these internal grading checks, and it keeps ratings fair by matching what the tool was actually asked to do.

ai.title: Bundle SDK for node target
ai.summary: SDK build switched to Bun bundler, generating dual ESM/CJS outputs with dynamic externals. Replaced tsup and manual package.json manipulation. Code-map updated to support runtime WASM loading via init-node.ts, removing static imports. Publish script simplified to build, verify, publish.

eli5.text: The code-map package now loads its language-parsing engine dynamically at runtime instead of bundling all the pieces together at build time, which means the WebAssembly files for each programming language are resolved on demand when you actually need them rather than being included unconditionally. This change is live today and primarily affects anyone using code-map's parsing features, who will see fewer upfront loading costs for language support they don't use. If you looked at the internals, you'd notice the bundle size for the core package is significantly smaller since the language-specific parsers are no longer statically imported.

ai.title: SDK 0.1.27 adds build verification to dry-run
ai.summary: The @codebuff/sdk package version bumps to 0.1.27. The publish-dry-run script now executes bun run build:verify before running the publish script. This change ensures build integrity checks are performed during dry-run publishing. The update is scoped to sdk/package.json.

eli5.text: The software development kit for building with Codebuff now runs a full check-up before testing a preview of its next public release. Previously, a dry run could report success even when the kit's contents had not been fully assembled and validated. Now, the system builds and verifies everything first, then performs the dry-run check, so any broken pieces are caught earlier. This only affects the behind-the-scenes packaging process used by the engineering team and has no impact on features available to you today.

ai.title: SDK types path fix and version bump to 0.1.28
ai.summary: Updated `@codebuff/sdk` version to 0.1.28. Corrected `types` and `exports.types` paths from `./dist/esm/index.d.ts` to `./dist/esm/sdk/src/index.d.ts` to resolve type resolution issues. Scope limited to `sdk/package.json`.

eli5.text: If you use Codebuff's developer tools to build AI-powered features, your tools will now correctly find the built-in instructions it provides for integration. Previously, a small navigation error made those instructions unreadable, which could leave your setup unable to recognize the available building blocks; that glitch is fixed. This is a behind-the-scenes correction limited to one configuration file, so most users won't notice any visible difference, but it keeps the developer setup stable for those building on top of Codebuff.

ai.title: README rewrite plus new agent guide and local dev docs
ai.summary: README.md rewritten around multi-agent architecture with new demo.gif and multi-agents.png assets. common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/agent-guide.md added as 211-line reference covering AgentDefinition structure, tool names, and handleSteps generator control flow. local-development.md added documenting Bun, direnv, Infisical, and Docker setup steps. npm-app/src/cli.ts touched alongside initial-agents-dir/README.md restructured for context-window rationale.

eli5.text: If you open Codebuff's main project page, you'll see a rewritten introduction and a short looping demo showing the tool in action, plus a new diagram explaining how it coordinates several AI agents at once instead of relying on a single helper. Anyone building custom workflows now has a step-by-step guide and clearer sample files describing how to define their own agents, choose which AI model they use, and mix automated steps with AI decisions. A separate setup guide was added explaining how to run Codebuff locally for development, covering the required tools and environment. The supporting command-line and agent-template files were adjusted to match the new documentation structure, so the published materials stay accurate as the system evolves.

ai.title: Add CI workflow to mirror initial-dot-agents templates
ai.summary: New GitHub Actions workflow mirrors `common/src/templates/initial-dot-agents` to a separate `.agents` repository via `git subtree push`. Triggered on pushes to `main` affecting the template directory. Requires `SUBTREE_PUSH_TOKEN` secret for authentication.

eli5.text: When someone updates the standard starter templates for AI agents in the main project, those template files now automatically get copied over to a separate shared repository that other teams and projects can pull from, no manual copying or syncing needed anymore. This keeps everyone using the same base set of agent instructions without someone having to remember to copy changes by hand. You wouldn't see this happening directly, but if you rely on those shared agent templates, your copies will now stay up to date automatically whenever the main project's starter files change. The system uses a secure token to authenticate the transfer, so only authorized updates are pushed through.

ai.title: Trailing newline in initial agents README
ai.summary: Added trailing newline to common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/README.md. Ensures POSIX compliance for the template file. Scope limited to core shared templates.

eli5.text: When you use the tool to create a fresh project, it drops in a starter guide file that explains how to get started. That guide was missing a final line break at the end, which is a small formatting rule most systems expect, so the team added it. If you looked at that guide file on disk, you'd now see a clean end to the text instead of the last line pressing right against the file's edge. This only affects new projects created from the built-in template, so existing work stays the same.

ai.title: Fix mirror-dot-agents workflow path
ai.summary: Updated .github/workflows/mirror-dot-agents.yml to reference common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir instead of initial-dot-agents. This aligns the git subtree push prefix with the actual directory structure. The workflow trigger paths and push command now correctly target the renamed template directory.

eli5.text: The system that publishes a shared set of pre-built helpers to a separate project now points to the right folder after that folder was renamed. If you looked at the publishing settings today, you'd see it targeting the correctly named directory that matches where the helpers actually live. This only affects the automated publishing of that specific shared helper set, not anything you do day to day.

ai.title: Fix mirror-dot-agents workflow target repo
ai.summary: CI workflow `.github/workflows/mirror-dot-agents.yml` updates `git subtree push` target from placeholder `ORG/SUBDIR-REPO` to actual `codebuffai/codebuff-dot-agents`. Fixes push failure caused by invalid remote URL. Scope limited to CI config and trailing newline in `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/README.md`.

eli5.text: You publish a set of agent templates from the main workspace into a shared public repository so that anyone installing the starter agents gets the latest version. That publishing step was trying to push to a fake placeholder address, so it was failing and your templates were not reaching the shared repository. It now pushes to the real shared repository address, so the latest templates should flow through within minutes of the next scheduled run. A trailing blank line was also added to the templates' readme file.

ai.title: mirror-dot-agents workflow token swap
ai.summary: mirror-dot-agents.yml uses CODEBUFF_GITHUB_TOKEN for git subtree push. Previous SUBTREE_PUSH_TOKEN likely failed or deprecated. Affects CI workflow and initial-agents-dir README trailing newline removal.

eli5.text: When the project's helper files get automatically copied to a separate repository, the copy step now uses CodeBuff's own publishing key instead of the old shared key that had stopped working. If you manage the CodeBuff organization on GitHub, the automated sync will succeed again and no longer fail midway. The template README that gets copied alongside it also had a stray blank line removed, so the pasted instructions end cleanly without a dangling empty line.

ai.title: Referral page fix, CLI-only redemption, OAuth code preservation
ai.summary: Referral redemption moved from web auto-redeem to CLI-only entry via handleReferralCode in npm-app/src/client.ts; web onboarding now shows install instructions instead of granting credits. New web/src/app/referrals/[code]/page.tsx server component fetches /api/referrals/[code] and renders invalid-code, self-referral, and claim states. OAuth referral codes preserved via absolute callback URLs plus localStorage fallback in SignInButton, with ReferralRedirect recovery component on home page catching missed referrals. auth-options.ts redirect callback now extracts referral_code param and forwards it to /onboard; onboard/page.tsx branches on authCode presence to separate CLI flow from web flow.

eli5.text: If you click or type a referral link on the website today, you'll see a page that tells you the code isn't applied online, instead it shows terminal-style install instructions for applying the code yourself in the Codebuff command-line app. Behind the scenes, the site now keeps your referral code safe while you sign in with Google or GitHub, and if it ever gets lost, a small recovery step on the home page catches it and finishes applying the credit for you. This only affects people signing up through a referral link; it doesn't change anything for users logging in normally without a code.

ai.title: Add tmate debug shell to mirror-dot-agents workflow
ai.summary: Commented out `paths` filter in `.github/workflows/mirror-dot-agents.yml` to trigger on all main pushes. Added `mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3` step gated by `failure()` with 15m timeout for SSH debugging. Scope limited to CI mirror workflow.

eli5.text: The system that keeps a backup copy of the assistant files in sync now runs every time anything is pushed to the main code branch, instead of only when specific files change. When that sync process breaks, it automatically opens a temporary remote terminal that developers can securely connect to in order to investigate what went wrong. This only affects the internal backup-copy process and not the assistant you interact with.

ai.title: mirror-dot-agents.yml: token guard, URL fix, remove tmate
ai.summary: mirror-dot-agents.yml adds a TOKEN existence check before git subtree push. Auth URL switched from x-access-token:${TOKEN} to ${TOKEN} for codebuff-dot-agents.git. Removed mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3 failure debug step. Scope: .github/workflows/mirror-dot-agents.yml only.

eli5.text: Nothing for you to see here. What changed: The small, automated process that copies a folder of starter agent setups into the shared agent gallery now checks for a required password before it runs, instead of silently failing partway through. It also sends that password in a slightly different format, and it no longer opens a hidden live-debug terminal window when something goes wrong. Who it helps: Internal maintainers who run that copying process. You probably ran it, and if the password was missing or misconfigured before, the copy would stop early. You might have seen an error in the logs; now you'll get a plain "token does not exist" line instead. The debug terminal that used to pop up on failure is gone, so if a run still fails, you'll just see a normal failure message and have to

ai.title: Improve token logging and auth in mirror workflow
ai.summary: Updated .github/workflows/mirror-dot-agents.yml to log first 10 chars of TOKEN and switch git auth to x-access-token. Replaced boolean existence check with cut command for partial token visibility. Ensures correct authentication method for codebuff-dot-agents mirror.

eli5.text: When the system mirrors its starter agent templates to a shared repository, it now prints only the first 10 characters of the secret access key used for publishing, instead of just confirming whether the key exists. This change affects anyone debugging mirror failures in the codebuff-dot-agents workflow, because they will see partial key text in the logs rather than a simple yes/no notice. The publishing step still runs today against the same shared repo, but now authenticates using the standard GitHub token format expected by the remote host.

ai.title: README updates add comparison image and clarify CLI steps
ai.summary: README.md adds assets/codebuff-vs-claude-code.png to visualize eval performance. Multi-agent diagram width reduced 600px to 250px. CLI section splits install and run commands into separate code blocks with explicit labels.

eli5.text: If you open the project's main guide, you'll now see a side-by-side chart showing how it stacks up against a rival tool, plus the opening paragraph no longer leads with the score. The opening paragraph no longer leads with the score. The setup steps that used to sit in one block are now split into two labeled sections, one for installing and one for running, so it's harder to mix up which command comes first. The picture that shows how the different parts work together has also been shrunk to roughly half its previous width so it doesn't push the rest of the page too far down.

ai.title: Remove token logging from mirror-dot-agents workflow
ai.summary: The `mirror-dot-agents.yml` workflow no longer logs the first 10 characters of the `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_TOKEN`. This removes a debugging step that exposed partial secret data in CI logs. The change applies to the `.github/workflows/mirror-dot-agents.yml` file.

eli5.text: The system that automatically copies certain project files stopped writing a short piece of its secret login code into the build logs when it runs. This means the logs generated during those automated file-copying runs will no longer contain even a partial snippet of the password used to push the files. This affects only the internal automation process, not any visible product feature.

ai.title: Hardened mirror-dot-agents CI workflow
ai.summary: Updated mirror-dot-agents.yml to disable persist-credentials and explicitly clear the default GitHub auth header via git config --global --unset-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader. Changed bot identity to codebuff mirror bot. This prevents credential leakage and ensures the workflow uses the injected CODEBUFF_GITHUB_TOKEN secret.

eli5.text: The automated process that copies agent files into the.agents directory now runs without saving login credentials and uses a dedicated bot account called 'codebuff mirror bot' instead of the default GitHub Actions bot. If you looked at the workflow, you'd see it explicitly clears any leftover GitHub authentication headers and disables credential persistence to ensure only the injected secret token is used. This is internal housekeeping with no visible effect on the product or its users.

ai.title: Referral flow updates: GitHub sign-in, self-referral handling, navbar
ai.summary: The referral page now uses a dedicated `GitHubSignInButton` for unauthenticated users instead of a generic login link, storing the referral code in `localStorage` as a fallback and capturing PostHog events. The inline 'same user' check was removed from `web/src/app/referrals/[code]/page.tsx`; the 'Complete Referral' button now only renders for logged-in users who are not the referrer. A 'Refer Friends' item linking to `/profile?tab=referrals` was added to `web/src/components/navbar/user-dropdown.tsx`.

eli5.text: When you visit someone else's referral page while signed in, you now see a GitHub sign-in button instead of a generic link if you're logged out. The page no longer shows a 'that's your own referral code' message inline; instead, the 'Complete Referral' button only appears for logged-in users who aren't the referrer. A new 'Refer Friends' link has been added to your profile dropdown in the navbar, and referral codes are saved in your browser when you sign in through the referral flow. These changes are live today across the web app.
